This role represents a shift from operational service management to system leadership, with responsibility for driving performance, service innovation, workforce capability, financial sustainability, and effective governance across the portfolio. Reporting to the General Manager, you will work closely with internal teams, government, and community partners to drive collaboration, strengthen service systems and translate strategy into meaningful outcomes. This is a full-time, permanent opportunity based at our Wodonga office. This newly created role offers a competitive salary package of $170,000 – $180,000, inclusive of fully maintained company vehicle and superannuation. This role can be based in either Wodonga or Wangaratta, however travel will be required between both sites and to our Shepparton office. What You Can Expect In the role, you will: Lead and influence the strategic direction and performance of Youth and Family Homelessness services. Lead the improvement and integration of homelessness services to create stronger pathways and outcomes for young people and families. Use data, insights, and evidence to drive continuous improvement and informed decision making. Provide strong leadership across workforce capability, financial performance, governance, and risk management. Build strategic partnerships and represent the organisation across government, community, and sector networks. Lead change and translate strategy into action to create meaningful outcomes for the community. About You You will bring: Demonstrated senior leadership experience with accountability for service delivery, performance and strategic outcomes within complex human services environments Strong capability in service improvement, financial management, workforce planning, and operational delivery. Experience building high-performing teams, strengthening leadership capability and workforce sustainability. Sound knowledge of governance, risk management and compliance frameworks. Proven ability to lead change and translate strategy into effective operational delivery. Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships across government, community, and sector partners. Relevant tertiary qualifications in a related discipline (e.g. social work, psychology, community services, management) or equivalent experience. A leadership, business, or management qualification, or a demonstrated willingness to undertake further study in a relevant leadership or business discipline. About Us Junction Support Services is an award-winning regional not-for-profit that has been empowering brighter futures for more than 35 years. We deliver trauma-informed housing, health, disability, education and family services across regional Victoria and NSW, supporting more than 2,500 people each year. What We Offer This role offers the opportunity to create meaningful change in your community. Join a team that values connection, growth and making a positive impact in people’s lives. Why Join Junction? Increase your take home pay with a generous salary packaging and fully maintained company vehicle Enjoy 5 weeks annual leave, with 17.5% leave loading on 4 of those weeks Ongoing professional development Clinical supervision and debriefing opportunities Supportive, inclusive culture where people thrive together Lead meaningful change and make a genuine difference every day How To Apply To apply, please click 'Apply' and submit: Your current resume, outlining your relevant skills, qualifications, and experience. A cover letter explaining why you are well suited to this role. A response to the key selection criteria, demonstrating how your skills, experience, and achievements align with the requirements of the position. Applications close: 27th September 2026. We look forward to receiving your application. If you have any questions about this opportunity, please contact the People & Culture team on (02) 6043 7400. Our Commitment to Diversity and Child Safety Junction Support Services is a child-safe organisation and an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from First Nations peoples, individuals with disability or lived experience of disability, and people of all cultural backgrounds, gender identities and sexual orientations. We value the unique perspectives and contributions that diversity brings to our workplace and the communities we serve.

We turn real company work into immersive virtual simulated internships where students complete professional missions, work with company resources, interact with AI managers, receive feedback and evaluation, and build verified evidence of what they can actually do. Our vision goes beyond courses and traditional job simulations. We are building an AI-powered environment where people can build experience, prove their abilities, and prepare for a rapidly changing world of work. About the Opportunity We are looking for an exceptional AI Engineer to join Owlera as a technical co-founder/founding technical partner and take ownership of the AI intelligence behind the platform. This is not a role focused on simply connecting an application to an LLM API. We need someone who can architect and build production AI systems that become core parts of the Owlera experience. You would work directly with the founder to transform our validated MVP into a scalable AI-powered platform and help shape both the product and technical direction of the company. What You'll Do You will design and build Owlera's AI architecture and core AI product capabilities, including: • AI agents and multi-step agentic workflows • AI Managers and Supervisors that guide students through realistic work experiences • AI evaluators that assess student submissions, provide feedback, score performance, and identify skills and professional behaviors • RAG systems that allow AI agents to understand company documents, resources, processes, and internship context • LLM integrations, orchestration, tool calling, memory, context management, and structured outputs • Conversational AI and intelligent chat experiences • AI-powered internship and mission generation from real company information • Career intelligence and personalized AI guidance • Reliable evaluation pipelines, guardrails, monitoring, testing, and AI quality improvement • Backend integrations required to connect these AI systems with the wider Owlera product You will also help determine what should be handled by agents, traditional software, retrieval systems, workflows, or other AI approaches as the platform scales. What We're Looking For We are looking for someone who is both a strong AI engineer and a builder. You should have hands-on experience with LLM applications, AI agents, agentic workflows, RAG, embeddings/vector databases, tool calling, structured outputs, prompt and context engineering, and production AI systems. Experience with Python and modern backend development is important. Full-stack experience is a major advantage because this is an early-stage company where technical ownership will extend beyond isolated AI models. Most importantly, we want someone who thinks like a founder: someone comfortable with ambiguity, fast experimentation, technical ownership, product decisions, and building from an early stage. Experience in EdTech, HRTech, Future of Work, assessment systems, recommendation systems, or AI evaluation is valuable but not required. Important: This Is a Co-Founder Opportunity This is not a salaried position at this stage. Owlera is currently pre-seed and raising capital. We are looking for a technical partner who believes in the problem and wants to help build the company from the ground up in exchange for co-founder equity, with compensation becoming possible as the company raises funding and grows. This opportunity is best suited for someone who wants more than their next engineering job. We are looking for someone who wants to help build the technology, product, team, and company alongside the founder. Learn more about Owlera: www.owlera.online
